The Map Beneath the Moon

Amara finds a silver map beneath her bedroom rug. By sunrise, she and a blue heron must find their way through a library in the clouds and bring home a missing star.

Read the whole storyMake one like this

Amara’s story

Read all ten spreads below, or open the page-turning reader.

A silver secret

At bedtime, Amara saw a silver glow beneath her rug. She pulled out a map. Moonlight ran across it like a bright river. At the window, a blue heron tapped its beak and pointed to one tiny boat.

The paper boat

Amara folded the map into a paper boat. It grew just large enough for her to climb inside. The moonlit river slipped through the sleeping garden. The heron flew beside her, quiet as a shadow.

The whispering wood

The river entered a dark forest. Every path looked the same. Amara lifted the map to the moon. Silver arrows appeared on the trees. “This way,” she said, and the heron nodded.

Three star locks

A stone door rose beside the river. It had three star-shaped locks. Amara studied the map and turned them from smallest to largest. Click, click, click. The old door opened.

The sky library

Beyond the door floated a library in the clouds. Curved ladders reached through the sky. Glowing books travelled like tiny planets. Amara stepped from her boat and stared. She had never seen so many stories.

The empty case

An old owl showed Amara an empty glass case. “The North Star should shine here,” he said. Without it, travellers could lose their way. The silver map pointed towards a maze of moving shelves.

The book maze

The shelves shifted around Amara. On the map were three pictures: a sun, a feather and a wave. She found each symbol in order. At once, the shelves opened to reveal a glowing staircase.

The storm nest

At the top of the tower, the North Star was tangled in dark storm threads. Wind pulled at Amara’s coat. She held the star steady while the heron loosened each knot with its long beak.

Light returns

Amara carried the star back to its case. Golden light raced through every shelf and window. Books opened. Ladders danced. The old owl cheered. Far below, silver paths shone across the world.

One last spark

The paper boat carried Amara home before sunrise. In her room, it became an ordinary map again. Almost ordinary. One small point still glowed. Whenever Amara needed courage, the North Star would remember her.
